gist: Atwood moves from the physicians' freeing of the hidden Light for bodily cure to the Theurgic and Hermetic freeing of the Mind, arguing through alchemical authorities that the work is rational, patient, experiential inquiry, and that its central operation, Separation, is done not mechanically but by Mind/Intellect (the 'Reason' or 'Intellectual sun', called Gold, Sol, Sulfur, Tincture), with natural reason serving only as an 'iron key'. She closes with Anaxagoras on Intellect as the unmixed separating power.

notes.point: Physicians freed the captive Light to cure the body; the Theurgic Art purified and informed the Mind, nearest of all to the regeneration preached by Jesus Christ: baptismal purification, then subjugation of passions and adaptation of lower powers to reason, then conversion of the whole hypostasis through faith into substant inner light.

To find this Reason the ancients questioned Nature rationally, not destructively like modern chemistry; knocking as bidden, they were admitted from within as lawful guests and, in the inner chamber, sought not phenomena but worthiness of nature's own light.
Theurgists consulted the divine intellect only on purification, liberation and the salvation of life, and things beneficial to life and truth.

Every entrant first wanders among chimeras and errors before experimental knowledge; rightly begun, inquiry traces the chain of vital causes to Deity, whence adepts worked supernatural effects below. Their only aim was the Central Light and Wisdom, until the hidden Divinity became manifest in experience.

Alchemists: examine patiently, infer from experience, follow God's Rule; do not ask nature beyond her strength but help her exceed her course; the Mercury of the Wise comes only by ingenuity and industry.
notes.voice: QUOTED: the Alchemists (Lumen de lumine; Lully)

notes.point: Crollius: holy assiduity of preparations, contemplation of causes, handiwork and infused grace bring forth more than nature promises. Van Helmont: the Tree of Life is laborious, fruit of intellectual research.
Basil Valentine: find nature's concealed first foundation with your own eyes and hand, or remain a phantastic trifler building on sand; adepts demand proofs by experience, not words.
Atwood: all adepts agree the way to Wisdom is patience and rational inquiry into the intimate causes of things.
Basil: the second part is celestial contemplation by spiritual reason: how nature is perfected by its own resolution, and how destruction and compaction separate pure from impure.

Natural reason is dull and inoperative here, only an iron key on the threshold; once it admits the spiritual intellect into self-knowledge, that intellect returns upon outer life and transforms it by the fiery essence of its new Law.

This vital perscrutinator (Eirenaeus' 'internal fire of the sulfur of thy water') operates the whole change; only its holders pass the narrow gate to the Magistery of life, as in the Mysteries. It is the flower of intellect triply imprisoned in the body; only a lover of Wisdom can free it.

Eirenaeus: our fire, sulfur of Gold and seed of gold, is imprisoned in the body; our water frees it by rotting the body (glossed: ethereal body); after separation of elements it appears in the Third Menstrual, unseen by those ignorant of the first two.

Practice: prepare the first water, join it to the body in just pondus, seal philosophically until the infant forms, govern fire so external heat cherishes internal, await signs; the water opens the body's pores and partly extracts the tincture of Sol. Mind the internal Fire over the Athanor's; Aries, Saturn, Mercury, Doves of Diana.

Parallels: the Sybil sends Aeneas for the Golden Bough, which yields to the fated, not to force; Orpheus leads the prudent to the Cave of Mercury, glossed as Taenerus, the most hidden vapor of life, whence the right-minded carry the mineral radix of the Art. Without right mind and the ordained order of operation, the power stays hidden in an uncongenial soul.
Fire loves fire, to assimilate gold, not make it: throw the true gold-body (not a brazen ferment) into a bottomless Mercury whose center it finds only by finding its own.
notes.voice: QUOTED: 'they' (Ripley Revived; Maier; Lumen de Lumine)

notes.point: The art of Oedipus subdues the Sphinx: the Ethereal Spirit abandons phantasy and yields clear understanding to the trained inquirer. Synesius: Intellect purifies phantastic Spirit and extends it to Divinity; natural Intellect cannot.

Language fails: the adepts' claim of mind's magic action, a freed will refining its own vehicle to universal intelligence, is hard for an age without experimental knowledge of causality; Atwood will nonetheless discuss it.

Paracelsus' Separation, 'the greatest miracle in philosophy', is identical with the Mysteries' ordeals in the death of natural life: suffering, dread, dissolution, corruption, resurrection of pure Ether into Light. It is the Art's primary object.

Paracelsus: the creature has free power in the work, free will is friend or foe, but the sequestatrix gives form and essence; Atwood: this is Intellect, Hermes' perscrutinating Intellect. The Smaragdine Tablet commands separating subtle from gross gently; the Asclepius says man can effect the Causal Nature.

Hence decomposition is not mechanical: Mind is the true Separator and regimen, admitting no foreign admixture; nothing is found unless the matter is decomposed and the whole introversion passed. Hermes: the matter is One only Thing.

Folly, phantasy, passion and Reason are modes of the One Thing; as phantasy converts all to folly, Reason ascendant ferments all into its Light, as Lully, Arnold, Bacon, Geber intimate of their Head Stone.

Ordinary reason, which separates fact from falsehood, and a standard subsisting by faith give a glimpse of the higher Reason, called Wisdom, Intellect, Gold, Sol, Sulfur, Tincture. It is Light; as the sun sublimes matter, the Intellectual sun archetypally rejects false forms, triturates foreign tincture, and infuses itself into the passified Spirit.

Anaxagoras (via Simplicius, Taylor) confirms: Intellect is infinite, unmingled, purest, all-knowing, ruling all soul; it separated dense from rare, hot from cold, lucid from dark, dry from moist; it alone is singular, and all Intellect is alike.

method.veiled: To find this Light, and to free it from captivity
method.plain: The work's object is a Light held captive; physicians freed it for bodily healing, the Theurgic Art for purifying and informing the Mind.

method.veiled: an effectual baptismal purification
method.plain: A first purifying step that 'prepared the way' before the passions were subdued.
method.basis: III.1 ¶11: 'by an effectual baptismal purification, they also prepared the way, and by a gradual subjugation...' places it first in sequence; its nature is not further specified.

method.veiled: a gradual subjugation of the passions and adaptation of the subordinate powers to reason
method.plain: Gradually bringing passions and lower faculties under the rule of reason.

method.veiled: the whole hypostasis was converted finally through faith into the identity of substant light within
method.plain: The person's whole being is finally changed, through faith, into an inner light with which it becomes identical.
method.basis: III.1 ¶11, final step of the stated sequence; 'hypostasis' read as the whole subject undergoing the work.

method.veiled: put the question to Nature rationally
method.plain: Inquire of nature by reason and courtesy, not by destructive analysis ('as is with modern chemistry the fashion, to demolish her edifices').

method.veiled: they knocked as was bid them, and the doors being opened from within
method.plain: Entry into the 'inner chamber' is granted from inside to those who ask as directed, not forced.
method.basis: III.1 ¶12 contrasts this with demolishing nature; 'lawful guests'; cf. ¶13 'narrow gate' and 'passport'.

method.veiled: sphered in the magian circle of her own light
method.plain: Nature, once entered, is found exalted above the inquirers in her own light, which they seek to become worthy to know.
method.basis: III.1 ¶12: 'become worthy of the knowledge and familiarity of that light'.

method.veiled: he wanders awhile in the region of chimeras
method.plain: Beginners make many erroneous inquiries before reaching experimental knowledge.

method.veiled: having set the chain of vital causes in action, succeeded in tracing them to their last efficient link in Deity
method.plain: Adepts activated a series of vital causes and followed it back to its divine origin, from which, under divine will, they could work supernatural effects below.

method.veiled: For the Central Light and Wisdom was all their aim
method.plain: The goal is the Central Light/Wisdom, sought until 'the hidden Divinity was moved into experience and made manifest in effect and power'.

method.veiled: you must help her, that she may exceed her common course, or all is to no purpose
method.plain: Nature alone does not produce the result; the operator's art must push her beyond her ordinary course.

method.veiled: the Mercury of the Wise comes not but by help of ingenuity and industry
method.plain: The 'Mercury of the Wise' is obtained only through the operator's skill and labor.

method.veiled: a holy assiduity of preparations
method.plain: Devout, persistent preparatory work, combined with contemplation of natural causes and manual experience, plus infused divine grace.

method.veiled: the attainment of the Tree of Life is laborious, and the fruit of intellectual research
method.plain: The goal is reached by hard work and intellectual inquiry.

method.veiled: the first foundation, says the monk, which nature holds concealed
method.plain: A hidden basis in nature that must be found by personal experience ('with thine own eyes and hand'), without which theorizing is 'built upon sand'.

method.veiled: how the destruction and compaction are to be handled
method.plain: Managing dissolution and recombination so that 'the pure may be separated from the impure', understood by 'spiritual reason'.

method.veiled: as it were an iron key, intended to unlock the golden treasury of light within
method.plain: Natural reason is necessary but only a threshold tool; it opens access to an inner light and to the spiritual intellect, which then does the real work.

method.veiled: returning with power upon the life without, proceeds to analyze and revolutionize
method.plain: Once in self-knowledge, the spiritual intellect turns back on outer life and transforms it, 'proving all... chemically by the fiery essence of its newly conceived Law'.

method.veiled: the internal fire of the sulfur of thy water
method.plain: Eirenaeus' name for the 'vital perscrutinator' (the awakened spiritual intellect) that 'operates the whole change'.

method.veiled: they only who have obtained this passport can attain to the Magistery of life
method.plain: Only those in whom this inner investigator has been awakened can complete the work; it is self-protecting against intruders ('the narrow gate').

method.veiled: the flower of human intellect, triply imprisoned in the dark body’s hold
method.plain: What is sought is the highest part of human intellect, hidden deep within the body; the philosopher's task is to free it.

method.veiled: he must be a lover of Wisdom who can set her free
method.plain: Only a genuine lover of Wisdom can free it.

method.veiled: Our fire is the true sulfur of Gold
method.plain: The 'fire' is a principle imprisoned in the hard dry body, called also 'the seed of gold'.

method.veiled: by the mediation of our water it is set loose, by rotting the moles of the body (i.e., of the ethereal body)
method.plain: A 'water' frees the fire by putrefying the body's masses; the bracketed gloss identifies that body as the ethereal body.
method.basis: III.1 ¶14 parenthetical glosses '(i.e., of the ethereal body)' and '(of the same body)' are inserted in Atwood's text; what 'our water' is, is not stated here.

method.veiled: it appears visibly in our Third Menstrual
method.plain: After separation of the elements the freed fire becomes visible at a third stage/solvent; the 'two first menstruals' must be known first.

method.veiled: to join it to the body in a just pondus
method.plain: Combine the prepared 'first water' with the 'body' in correct proportion.

method.veiled: to shut it up in its vessel philosophically, until the infant be formed
method.plain: Seal the mixture in its vessel and leave it until a new product ('infant') forms.

method.veiled: to govern his fire dexterously, so as to cherish internal heat with external
method.plain: Regulate applied heat so it nourishes the inner heat; called 'greater than all'.

method.veiled: can wait with patience till he sees signs
method.plain: Patience until signs appear; the first sign of progress is the water opening the body's pores and partly extracting 'the tincture of Sol'.

method.veiled: be not so careful of the fire of the Athanor as of your internal Fire
method.plain: The inner fire matters more than the furnace's external fire.

method.veiled: Seek it in the house of Aries, and draw it from the depths of Saturn
method.plain: Where to find the internal Fire; not explained in this chunk.
method.basis: III.1 ¶14: 'it' follows 'your internal Fire'; no gloss of Aries or Saturn given. See ambiguities.

method.veiled: your signal the Doves of Diana
method.plain: A named sign or signal in the work; its meaning is not given here.

method.veiled: well directing him how to look from beneath upwards, and take it in hand
method.plain: Aeneas' search for the Golden Bough is offered as a parallel errand: look upward, take it in hand; it yields willingly only to the fated, never to force or iron.
method.basis: III.1 ¶15 'On some such errand' links it to the preceding search; ¶16 Latin (our translation) on force being useless.

method.veiled: the Cave of Mercury, which, according to the Hermetic interpretation, is Taenerus, the most hidden vapor of life
method.plain: The 'Cave of Mercury' means the most hidden vital vapor; from it is taken 'the mineral radix and true mater of the Hermetic Art'.

method.veiled: let him enter with a prudent motive, well understanding and allied to what he seeks
method.plain: The operator must have right motive, understanding and affinity with the object sought.

method.veiled: the power will remain hidden, despite of every effort, in a pusillanimous uncongenial soul
method.plain: Without a right mind and observance of 'the predestined conditions and the order of operation', effort fails.

method.veiled: Fire loves fire, say they, not to make gold, but to assimilate it
method.plain: The active principle works by assimilating like to itself, not by manufacturing.

method.veiled: Take, therefore, that body which is gold (not a brazen ferment), and throw it into Mercury
method.plain: Put the true gold-body (not a base substitute) into Mercury.

method.veiled: such a Mercury as is bottomless, or whose center it can never find, but by discovering its own
method.plain: The Mercury is unfathomable; the gold reaches its center only by finding its own center.

method.veiled: This is the art of Oedipus which, well conducted with the Sphinx, ends in her subjugation
method.plain: Atwood glosses it: 'the Ethereal Spirit abandons her phantasy, and yields the clear light of understanding' to the properly trained inquirer.

method.veiled: Intellect above all things separates whatever is contrary to the true purity of phantastic Spirit
method.plain: Intellect purifies the imaginative spirit, refining it and extending it to Divinity; natural intellect cannot.

method.veiled: the efficient force of an individual freed will upon the vehicle of its motive cause
method.plain: A freed individual will acting on its own vehicle, 'separating, refining, and transmuting it from an impure, dull consistency to the clear light of universal intelligence'.

method.veiled: Separation is the greatest miracle in philosophy
method.plain: Separation is 'the primary object of the Art', identical with the separation undergone in the Mysteries during 'the decomposition and death of the natural life'.

method.veiled: suffering, succedent dread, dissolution, and corruption, to the final resurrection of the pure Ether into Light
method.plain: Sequence of the Separation, paralleling the Mysteries' ordeals: suffering, dread, dissolution, corruption, then resurrection of the pure Ether as Light.

method.veiled: the sequestatrix, which gives to every thing its form and essence
method.plain: The separating power; Atwood identifies it as 'the part especial of Intellect'. Free will may be 'friend or foe' in the work.

method.veiled: Thou shalt separate the earth from the fire, the subtle from the gross, gently, with much sagacity
method.plain: Gentle, intelligent separation of subtle from gross; Atwood reads the Separator as Mind.

method.veiled: it will ascend from earth to heaven, and again descend from heaven to earth, and will receive the strength of the Inferiors and of the Superiors
method.plain: The separated subtle part rises and returns, gaining power from both above and below; not further glossed here.
method.basis: III.1 ¶21: follows the separation command in the Tablet citation; called 'the strong fortitude of all fortitudes'.

method.veiled: we observe Mind to be the true Separator, the efficient as well as the regimen of the work
method.plain: Mind both causes and governs the work; the 'decomponency of life' is not mechanical or ordinary dissolution.

method.veiled: no foreign admixture is allowed to enter
method.plain: Nothing external is added to the work.

method.veiled: nothing is discovered except the matte be decomposed
method.plain: The matter must be decomposed before anything is revealed, and the work is not perfected 'unless the whole introversion is passed through'.

method.veiled: the whole matter I know to be One only Thing
method.plain: The material of the work is a single thing; folly, phantasy, passion and Reason are its modes.
method.basis: III.1 ¶21 following sentence: 'folly, and phantasy, and passion are modes of being of the One Thing, and Reason is another'.

method.veiled: this Reason gaining the ascendancy, would gather all up, as a ferment, into the superior essence and traction of her own Light
method.plain: When Reason dominates the One Thing, it converts the rest into its own Light as a ferment converts dough, the reverse of phantasy converting all to folly.

method.veiled: abundantly celebrating the virtues of their Head Stone
method.plain: The 'Head Stone' celebrated by Lully, Arnold, Bacon, Geber is what Atwood links to Reason fermenting all into Light.
method.basis: III.1 ¶21: 'This Lully intimates; and Arnold, and Bacon, and Geber... celebrating the virtues of their Head Stone' directly follows the ferment sentence.

method.veiled: the Intellectual sun
method.plain: Supernatural Reason, which does essentially what natural reason does as image: rejects 'false forms and elementary qualities which supervene through generation', assimilates inferior life by 'continual trituration of its foreign tincture', and perfects deficient faculties 'by pure infusion of Itself to the passified Spirit'.

method.veiled: separated the dense from the rare, the hot from the cold, the lucid from the dark, and the dry from the moist
method.plain: Intellect, unmixed and alone, is the power that separates contraries; cited to confirm Intellect's 'efficient operation'.

sources.use: Illustrates (apparently) natural Intellect's inability to effect the change.

ambiguities.quote: in order to discover this Reason
readings: 'this Reason' refers back to the Light of ¶11
it refers to reason as the power to which the passions were adapted in ¶11
ambiguities.basis: ¶11 ends with 'adaptation of the subordinate powers to reason' and 'substant light'; ¶21 later says of the Reason 'For it is Light indeed'.

ambiguities.quote: Take counsel; be not so careful of the fire of the Athanor as of your internal Fire
ambiguities.basis: No quotation marks; footnote (16) follows the whole paragraph, supporting reading 1; the shift to 'Take counsel' and 'your' could mark a new speaker.

ambiguities.quote: Seek it in the house of Aries, and draw it from the depths of Saturn
readings: astrological/planetary cover-names for where the internal Fire is found, unexplained in this chunk
ambiguities.basis: Only 'it' = 'your internal Fire' is recoverable from ¶14; no gloss given.

ambiguities.quote: your signal the Doves of Diana
readings: a sign of progress to watch for
a sign/ingredient tied to 'Mercury be the internal'
ambiguities.basis: ¶14 only; called 'signal', just after 'wait with patience till he sees signs'.

ambiguities.quote: such a Mercury as is bottomless, or whose center it can never find, but by discovering its own
readings: the gold-body can penetrate the Mercury only by finding its own center (self-discovery)
the Mercury is unfathomable, i.e. inexhaustible
ambiguities.basis: ¶19 wording; ¶13 'self-knowledge' of the spiritual intellect lends some support to reading 1.

ambiguities.quote: Salt is good, but if the Salt have lost its savor wherewith shall it be seasoned?
readings: natural Intellect, lacking the needed penetrative essence, cannot restore what is lost
a warning about loss of the inner virtue in the operator
ambiguities.basis: Placed immediately after 'neither is its essence so acutely penetrative as to operate the change required' (¶20); no gloss.

ambiguities.quote: triply imprisoned in the dark body’s hold
readings: three layers of enclosure, possibly related to the three menstruals of ¶14
ambiguities.basis: ¶13 gives no count of layers; ¶14 mentions 'many links' and three menstruals.

readings: the imprisoned fire/seed of gold of ¶14
ambiguities.basis: ¶15 'On some such errand' links it generally to the preceding search without naming the referent.

translations.translation: shut away, it sits farther off (the book continues: 'it is far off, gotten in the penetralia')

translations.original: Alte vestiga oculis: et rite repertum, Carpe manu; namque Ipse volens facilisaque sequetur, Si te fate vocant; aliter, non viribus ullis Vincere, nec duro poteris convellere ferro
translations.translation: Search on high with your eyes, and when it is duly found, pluck it with your hand; for it will follow of itself, willing and easy, if the fates call you; otherwise you will not be able to overcome it by any strength, nor tear it away with hard iron.

translations.original: At quaecunque virum ducit prudnetia cordis Mercurii ingedier spuluncam plurima ubi ille Deponit bona, stat quorum praegrandis acervus Ambabus valet hic minibus sibi sumere, et ista Ferre domum, valet hic vistare incommoda cuncta.
translations.translation: But whatever man prudence of heart leads to enter the cave of Mercury, where he lays down very many goods, of which a very great heap stands, this man can take them for himself with both hands and carry them home; this man can avoid all troubles. (¶19 gives the book's interpretive paraphrase.)

translations.original: Nescit Sol comitis non memor esse sui
translations.translation: The Sun does not know how to be unmindful of its companion.

translations.original: Ignire ignis amat, non aurificare sed, aurum.
translations.translation: Fire loves fire, say they, not to make gold, but to assimilate it.

translations.original: Intellectus naturam habens subtilem ad intelligendum res intelligibles, participat, cum entibus intensis et cum entibus extensis, viz., cum intenso calore corporis, cum quo conjunctus est et cum intense bonitate sustentata in suis intensis concretis
translations.translation: Intellect, having a subtle nature for understanding intelligible things, participates with intensive beings and with extensive beings, namely with the intense heat of the body to which it is joined, and with the intense goodness sustained in its intense concretes.

threads.note: 'this Light' refers back to the preceding chunk's discussion of the hidden fire/medicine freed by physicians.
Lully, Michael Maier and others: 'to which in the Practice we shall have occasion to allude' (forward to the Practice, Part IV).
Entry 'through the narrow gate, as in the Mysteries we have already described' (back to the Mysteries chapters).
Atwood announces she will go on to 'discuss the point' and 'substantialize without deforming this Intellectual Science' (forward).
'in a former citation from his book to the Athenians, Paracelsus' (back to an earlier citation of Paracelsus on Separation).
Separation identical with that 'described as taking place in the Mysteries' during 'the great ordeals' (back to Mysteries chapters).
'as before shown, no foreign admixture is allowed to enter' (back to an earlier demonstration).
Anaxagoras extract introduced at end of ¶21 continues in ¶22 (chunk ends with it).
